svg.title: How big does the rock need to be?
svg.text: The same site plan on a bigger rock
map.json re-evaluated at rock_run = 70, 90, 97, 110, at the scale of the other sheets, with every part expanded at the box each size gives it
The rock’s plan size is the one number in map.json the brief does not fix: 70 is a reading of the compactness sentence, not a fact of record. These
are the ruler beside it. 90 is the mid-point; 97 is where the brief’s own belfry sightline runs out (80 + 97 = 177 m); 110 is past it, and is drawn so
that being past it is visible.
the rock subtends 25.3° from the belfry
(27° reads as one object; 18° as an object in its setting)
the rock subtends 20.2° from the belfry
(27° reads as one object; 18° as an object in its setting)
the rock subtends 18.9° from the belfry
(27° reads as one object; 18° as an object in its setting)
the rock subtends 16.8° from the belfry
(27° reads as one object; 18° as an object in its setting)
REFUSED by the brief’s own bound
every zone expanded at the box each rock size gives it, at rock_run 70 to 140, one block at a time
From rock 70 to rock 140 — twice the rock, four times its plan area — the set of parts that build does not change. It is the cliff
road, at every size, and nothing else.
The plan halves the rock’s depth, halves it again, and halves it again, so the hall and the tower each get an eighth of it: 9
blocks at rock 70, 12 at rock 90, 18 at rock 140. The tower declares 125. Growing the rock grows an eighth of it.
Z0 never moves at all: the flat’s box is 40 × 8 × 80 at every rock size, because both its plan numbers are brief facts and its
height is tide_y + road_y. It refuses on height, and the rock cannot reach it.
So the rock’s size is not what is stopping anything, and “is 70 × 70 big enough” has no answer in the direction it is asked. What
the parts are too big for is the SUBDIVISION, not the rock.
